insights.headline: Gold pinned below $3,950 as strong US data and midterms loom; central banks bought 320t in Q3
insights.summary: Spot gold hovered near $3,930 on Tuesday as stronger-than-expected US jobs data lifted Treasury yields and reinforced December Fed-hike bets, while investors awaited the US midterm results. Offsetting the gloom, WGC data showed central banks bought 320 tonnes in Q3, up 42% on the year, even as high prices pushed India’s gold demand to a six-year-low trajectory and grey-market imports hit a three-year high.
points: Spot gold near $3,924 and silver ~$49.45 in late US trade as September US job openings beat estimates at 7.523m, pushing the 10-year yield toward 4.95% (Kitco).
Gold eased to ~$3,930 in early Asian trade on firmer dollar and yields, with traders awaiting midterm results; a Democratic House could support gold (FXStreet).
Central banks bought ~320t in Q3, +42% y/y and the fastest since late 2024, offsetting record-weak jewellery demand (InvestingLive, Mint/McGeever).
India’s Q3 gold demand fell 29% to 162.5t; informal imports jumped over 1,500% to 50t after the 15% duty hike, a three-year high (GJEPC, BusinessLine).
MCX gold fell ~Rs 1,400/10g and silver ~Rs 4,300/kg on Tuesday; rupee firmed for a third session to 94.75/$ (Economic Times, Business Standard).

brief.headline: Gold slips toward $3,900 as US yields climb
brief.summary: MCX gold fell Rs 1,400 per 10 g as rising US yields and near-77% December Fed-hike bets weighed; midterms in focus.

bullets.text: MCX gold fell about Rs 1,400 per 10 g and silver about Rs 4,300 per kg on Tuesday; spot gold eased toward $3,900.
Rising US Treasury yields and about 77% December Fed-hike bets kept pressure on gold as US midterm voting got underway.

trending.title: Election-day pressure: jobs data and midterms keep gold under $3,950
trending.summary: Stronger US labor data lifted Treasury yields and hardened December Fed-hike bets while gold eased to about $3,930 in early Asian trade, with traders watching the midterm vote for fiscal-policy clues.

trending.title: Central banks step up: 320t of Q3 buying, fastest since late 2024
trending.summary: Official buyers added ~320 tonnes in Q3, up 42% on the year, offsetting record-weak jewellery demand — a bright spot McGeever says is overshadowed by gold’s liquidity-driven selloffs.

trending.title: India’s demand slump and the 50-tonne grey market
trending.summary: WGC data shows India’s Q3 demand fell 29% to 162.5 tonnes while informal imports jumped over 1,500% to 50 tonnes after import levies rose to 15%, a three-year high.

trending.title: MCX metals slide as festive buying meets rate-hike bets
trending.summary: MCX gold fell about Rs 1,400/10g and silver about Rs 4,300/kg on Tuesday, with silver futures at their lowest since late 2025, even as the rupee firmed to 94.75 per dollar.

items.title: Gold, silver decline as strong U.S. jobs data lifts yields on election day - Kitco PM Report
items.summary: Spot gold and silver fell in late US trading on Tuesday as stronger-than-expected US labor data — September job openings rose to 7.523m vs ~7.15m expected — lifted Treasury yields and reinforced bets on further Fed tightening, Kitco reports. Spot gold held near $3,924/oz (-0.55%); silver slid 2.1% to ~$49.45, with traders also positioning for the midterm results.

items.title: Gold declines below $3,950 on stronger US Dollar, US midterm elections in focus
items.summary: Gold slipped to near $3,930 in early Asian trade on Wednesday, pressured by a firmer dollar and higher Treasury yields as traders awaited US midterm results for fiscal-policy clues, FXStreet reports. Commerzbank called the slide excessive: gold fell 3.7% on Friday to $3,870, its lowest in over a year, while a December Fed hike looks “highly likely”.

items.title: MCX gold prices fall Rs 1,400/10 gram, silver tanks Rs 4,300/kg ahead of Diwali while rate hike bets linger. What should you do?
items.summary: Gold futures on the MCX slipped about Rs 1,400 per 10 grams and silver futures tumbled roughly Rs 4,300 per kg in Tuesday's session ahead of Diwali, with expectations of further US rate hikes keeping pressure on the metals. The report notes the slide comes during peak festive buying and walks through the factors Indian buyers are weighing.

items.title: Central bank gold buying jumps 42% in Q3 as high prices hit jewellery demand, WGC says
items.summary: Central banks bought ~320 tonnes in Q3, up 42% on the year and ~675t so far in 2026, the WGC said — offsetting a 17% slump in jewellery consumption to ~310t, the weakest Q3 in the series, and a 19% fall in bar and coin demand. Gold averaged ~$4,260/oz; total demand was ~1,370t (-1%), with YTD demand level with 2025’s record.

items.title: ROI-As markets sway, safe havens shine. Except gold: McGeever
items.summary: Reuters’ Jamie McGeever argues gold, “the oldest safety play of all,” has failed to find a bid despite a risk-off backdrop reviving Treasuries, the dollar, franc and yen: gold is below $4,000/oz, down 9% YTD and ~10% under its 200-day average. An IMF paper found bullion is not a “reliable” hedge against equity volatility; central-bank buying (+42% in Q3 to 321t) is the bright spot.

items.title: Gold eases ahead of US midterm elections
items.summary: Spot gold fell 0.5% to $3,926.52 an ounce by 0353 GMT after a 2%+ rebound, as investors awaited the US midterm results; December futures dropped 0.8% to $3,936.30. KCM Trade's Tim Waterer said gold stays in consolidation mode and is being sold to cover losses elsewhere rather than bought as a haven. Traders see a 74% December Fed-hike chance (CME FedWatch); spot silver slipped 1.8% to $49.71.

items.title: Gold (XAUUSD), Silver, Platinum Forecasts – Gold Pulls Back As Selling Resumes
items.summary: Gold slipped again on Tuesday as rising Treasury yields — the 2-year above 4.61% and the 10-year above 4.95% — and near-77% December Fed-hike bets outweighed the pullback in oil prices ahead of the US midterm vote, FXEmpire reports. Spot gold was testing the $3,890–$3,910 support zone, while silver slid back toward $50 as the gold-silver ratio climbed above 79.

items.title: Silver prices crash ₹8,500/kg, gold drops ₹2,000/10g as US-Iran tensions revive inflation fears; is more fall ahead?
items.summary: December silver futures on MCX resumed their losing streak on Tuesday after reports of a US strike on Iran's Qeshm Island sent crude higher, reviving inflation fears and rate-hike expectations. Silver futures slipped ₹8,528 per kg to their lowest since late November 2025, while gold fell ₹2,000 per 10 grams, erasing Monday's brief rebound.

items.title: India's tax hike drives illegal gold imports to 3-year high
items.summary: The World Gold Council says India's informal gold imports surged more than 1,500% to 50 tonnes in the September quarter, from 3 tonnes a year earlier, the highest since 2023, citing Metals Focus data. The grey market has flourished since May's duty hike to 15%, and jewellers are holding back on restocking ahead of Diwali while more households buy for cash without invoices.

items.title: India's Gold Demand Falls 29% in Q3 as High Prices Restrain Buying
items.summary: India's gold demand fell 29% year-on-year to 162.5 tonnes in Q3 2026 as record-high prices curbed buying, WGC said. Jewellery demand dropped 20% to 99.9 tonnes; bar and coin buying fell 40% to 55 tonnes. In value terms demand still rose 3% to ₹2.42 lakh crore on an average Q3 price of $4,262 an ounce (₹1,48,891 per 10g). WGC pegs 2026 full-year demand at 625–675 tonnes, a six-year low.

items.title: Gold ETF inflows slow to ₹3,300 crore in October as AMCs suspend FoFs
items.summary: Gold ETFs drew an estimated ₹3,300 crore in October, down from September’s seven-month high of ₹4,450 crore, as most AMCs suspended fresh subscriptions to gold fund of funds in the second half of October following a Sebi direction linked to rising gold imports and rupee pressure. Analysts quoted say gold stays under pressure from Fed rate-hike expectations, a strong dollar and rising bond yields.

items.title: Rupee extends gains for third day, settles at 94.75 against the dollar
items.summary: The rupee strengthened for a third straight session, settling at 94.75 per dollar after opening at 94.68 versus a 94.90 previous close, supported by foreign fund inflows into domestic equities. Gains were capped by rebounding crude — Brent rallied to $106.07 a barrel after a US attack on Iran — and the currency has gained 1.14% so far this quarter on regulatory measures.
